positioning: The bird dog that springs first and apologizes never.
story: The Springer does not walk into a field. It springs into it. Every part of the breed is built for that first burst.

The name tells the job. In England, spaniels worked ahead of the hunter and sprang, or flushed, game birds from cover. The Springer did it with a wagging tail and a face that said this was the best day ever.
Cockers and field spaniels were once born in the same litters. Size and work sorted them out. The Springer became the bigger, longer-legged one.

The breed later split in two. A leaner field type stayed in the woods. A fuller-coated show type moved to the ring. Today they can look like different dogs with one name. The AKC recognized the breed in 1910.
At home the Springer is sunny, eager, and sticky. It follows you from room to room. It wants a job and your company. Left alone too long, it grows anxious.
Give it a long walk, a stick to carry, and a family to love. A Springer will take it from there.
rank_cap: The flushing spaniel that springs game (AKC)
fblocks: From its job of springing, or flushing, game birds out of cover. Cockers and field spaniels once shared its litters.
A leaner field type and a fuller-coated show type drifted so far apart that they look like different dogs. Both are Springers.
Needs daily exercise and a job. Can grow anxious when left alone. Long ears need regular checks and cleaning.
A feathered double coat, usually liver and white or black and white, sometimes with tan points. Made to shed water and push through brush.
Nineteen to twenty inches tall. Recognized by the AKC in 1910. Five to seven puppies to a litter.
days: Easter morning, a basket of dyed eggs, and one dog guarding one egg.
Springers can work all day. The breed was made for brush and water, dawn to dusk.
Millie, a Springer in the Bush White House, “wrote” a bestselling book.
Springers work as detection dogs. A flushing nose is a finding nose.
Greet every duck as a friend. Most will disagree. Keep wagging.
Field and show Springers share a name. Side by side, they look like two breeds.
A puppy asleep in an upturned flat cap, and a weathered hand that does not dare move.
last_walk:
The Easter basket is empty, and the evening is quiet.
Barley lies by the garden path, the last egg between his paws. A cottage window glows. A Springer’s day is built from big moments. This is the small one, the long breath after, when everyone is home and nobody has to move.
